newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BETIS ACCUSED OF THROWING GAME TO HARM RIVALS SEVILLA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BETIS ACCUSED OF THROWING GAME TO HARM RIVALS SEVILLA.

text.p: The players and coach of Spanish side Real Betis have hit back at critics who accused them of not trying in Saturday's 1-0 defeat by Sporting Gijon, a result that helped condemn local rivals Sevilla to relegation.
"We can't have a load on our conscience because of the poor seasons of others," said coach Serra Ferrer.
During the game Betis fans cheered the Sporting goal and booed offside decisions made against the visitors.
The match attracted a flood of criticism, principally from managers of other teams threatened by relegation.
"I had to turn the television off. I had never seen a team go out to lose," said Maximo Hernandez of Rayo Vallecano.
"Betis will pay in time. History doesn't forgive ... they will pay for it," said Espanyol's Paco Flores.
Betis captain Alexis Trujillo was quick to reply to the attacks.
"They are excuses to remove importance from their defeats," said Trujillo, "The fans' reaction was justified because they had to suffer a lot of pain in recent years."
After years of playing second fiddle to their neighbours, Betis have already qualified for Europe and reached the Spanish Cup final.
Sevilla, who have twice in the past been accused of throwing games to harm Betis, are former winners of the cup and league and have been perennial UEFA Cup hopefuls in recent years.
But the club have struggled since narrowly escaping relegation to the third division for accountancy irregularities in the summer of 1995.

A series of boardroom scandals unleashed by the incident has coincided with a run of bad luck on the field. The problems saw both Brazilian striker Bebeto and Argentine manager Carlos Bilardo come and go during the season.
